title: Scaling Attention via Feature Sparsity
claim: Our sparse approach reaches dense-level quality at lower latency, compute and memory, giving a better efficiency-accuracy trade-off.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side: line plot left, grouped bar chart right with dual axes
description: Two plots sit side by side, with a consistent blue (full attention baseline) versus pink (ours, SFA) color scheme. Panel (a), titled 'Latency comparison', is a line chart of validation perplexity against context length. The blue full-attention curve starts high at about 21 perplexity and declines to about 16. The pink star-marked SFA curve sits below it and reaches the same perplexity at much shorter latency. Panel (b), 'FLOPs & KV-cache comparison', is a grouped bar chart over activation dimension k (Base, 32, 16, 8). Solid bars show FLOPs on the left axis and hatched bars show KV-cache on the right axis. Pink SFA bars fall steadily below the tall blue baseline bars. A legend explains the fill patterns and colors. The eye goes first to the blue-versus-pink contrast.
caption: Overview of our proposed method. (a) Trade-off between performance and speed. Compared to directly reducing dimensionality with short embeddings, our method achieves a more favorable balance, delivering a 259% speedup over the original dimensionality while improving performance by 21.4% relative to the short-embedding baseline. (b) Computational and memory efficiency comparison. Our method reduces KV-cache memory usage by 41% and FLOPs by 49%.
abstract: Scaling Transformers to ultra-long contexts is bottlenecked by the $O(n^2 d)$ cost of self-attention. Existing methods reduce this cost along the sequence axis through local windows, kernel approximations, or token-level sparsity, but these approaches consistently degrade accuracy. In this paper, we instead explore an orthogonal axis: feature sparsity. We propose Sparse Feature Attention (SFA), where queries and keys are represented as $k$-sparse codes that preserve high-dimensional expressivity while reducing the cost of attention from $Î(n^2 d)$ to $Î(n^2 k^2/d)$. To make this efficient at scale, we introduce FlashSFA, an IO-aware kernel that extends FlashAttention to operate directly on sparse overlaps without materializing dense score matrices. Across GPT-2 and Qwen3 pretraining, SFA matches dense baselines while improving speed by up to $2.5\times$ and reducing FLOPs and KV-cache by nearly 50\%. On synthetic and downstream benchmarks, SFA preserves retrieval accuracy and robustness at long contexts, outperforming short-embedding baselines that collapse feature diversity. These results establish feature-level sparsity as a complementary and underexplored axis for efficient attention, enabling Transformers to scale to orders-of-magnitude longer contexts with minimal quality loss. Code is available at https://github.com/YannX1e/Sparse-Feature-Attention.
